study.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Periodic and Aperiodic Brain Activity Under Peripheral Nerve Stimulation With Acupuncture
study.journal: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
study.study_design: within-subject experimental study recording EEG during resting state and two acupuncture manipulation conditions
study.population: Twenty subjects aged 21-26 (mean age 23, 11 males and 9 females), who had no experience of acupuncture treatment and no significant difference in physical condition
study.inclusion_criteria: no experience of acupuncture treatment; no significant difference in physical condition; underwent comprehensive nervous system examination; no other neurological or psychological disorders, neuroactive drugs or any other factors that might affect EEG activity; met the criteria for acupuncture and agreed to participate
study.exclusion_criteria: neurological or psychological disorders; neuroactive drugs or any other factors that might affect EEG activity

conditions.scan_context: needle inserted into ST36 acupoint; lifting-thrusting manipulation performed for 1 minute

conditions.scan_context: needle inserted into ST36 acupoint; twirling-rotating manipulation performed for 1 minute

neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 20 seconds selected per condition per subject
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: finite impulse response bandpass filter from 0.5 Hz to 45 Hz
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: periodic power (a, log10 power of Gaussian peaks)

additional_methods.eeg_system: international 10-20 standard electrodes system, including 60 electrodes evenly distributed along the scalp and 4 electrooculography (EOG) electrodes
additional_methods.psd_method: Classical Welch method; Hamming window of 1 second with 50% overlap
additional_methods.fooof_parameters: peak width limits between 0.5 and 12, peak threshold of 2.0, 'fixed' background mode
additional_methods.artifact_correction: ICA for EOG artifacts; channels with correlation >50% with EOG electrodes subtracted; artifactual channels interpolated; baseline correction applied
additional_methods.classifier: support vector machine (SVM) for acupuncture manipulation decoding
additional_methods.pearson_correlation: used for aperiodic slope vs offset correlation analysis (both parameters confirmed normally distributed)

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Periodic parameters of delta frequency band: periodic power comparison across states
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: within-subject comparison across three states (rest, LT, TR)
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: FOOOF parameterization; statistical comparison (test not specified)
contrasts.narrative_result: The periodic parameters of delta frequency band did not significant differ between three states (periodic power: p = 0.97; p = 0.76)

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Neural entrainment: delta peaks at 1.5 Hz (acupuncture stimulation frequency) in frontal and central regions

contrasts.analysis_method_exact: FOOOF parameterization; inspection of periodic fitted curves
contrasts.neuroimaging_metric_exact: periodic peaks at delta band center frequency of 1.5 Hz
contrasts.narrative_result: the number of delta peaks at the center frequency of 1.5 Hz (the same frequency as acupuncture stimulation) significantly increased during acupuncture; power of delta band was mainly distributed in the left frontal lobe region, with a pronounced effect under the stimulation of LT manipulation; spectral peak in delta band emerges in frontal and central brain regions indicates a typical phenomenon of neural entrainment

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Center frequency of theta peaks: rightward shift after acupuncture stimulation
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: within-subject comparison: acupuncture vs resting state
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: FOOOF parameterization; statistical comparison

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Number of theta peaks decreased during acupuncture state vs resting state

contrasts.analysis_method_exact: FOOOF parameterization; inspection of periodic fitted curves
contrasts.narrative_result: the number of theta peaks decreased during acupuncture state with respect to the resting state; the distribution and power of theta rhythms decrease significantly

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Periodic power of alpha band: significantly higher after acupuncture stimulation vs resting state

contrasts.analysis_method_exact: FOOOF parameterization; statistical comparison
contrasts.narrative_result: the periodic power values of the alpha band were significantly higher after acupuncture stimulation compared to that during the resting state with p < 0.001; alpha periodic power was higher during acupuncture throughout the brain, especially on the occipital and right parietal lobe regions; TR manipulation demonstrated a stronger enhancement effect and a broader enhancement range compared with LT

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Beta band bandwidth: significantly decreased under LT manipulation
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: within-subject comparison: LT vs resting state
contrasts.timepoint_exact: during LT manipulation vs resting state
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: FOOOF parameterization; statistical comparison
contrasts.narrative_result: the bandwidth and the center frequency were significantly decreased under stimulation of LT manipulation, but no consistent alterations were observed between groups of LT and TR manipulations

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was used. This is a real acupuncture vs resting state comparison only. No blinding was described or assessed.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported at any point.

Deqi and sensory responses were not quantified with a validated instrument (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire). Only narrative descriptions of sensations (heaviness, numbness, distension) were provided.
Adverse events were not reported. It is unclear whether any adverse events occurred.

The specific statistical test used for comparing periodic and aperiodic parameters across conditions (e.g., paired t-test, Wilcoxon) was not explicitly named in the text. Only p-values and significance levels are reported.
No multiple comparison correction method was reported for the electrode-level or frequency-band-level comparisons.
The needle type (e.g., gauge, brand) was not specified.

The study design involves within-subject conditions (resting state, LT, TR), but it is unclear whether the order of LT and TR was randomized or counterbalanced across subjects, or whether each subject received both manipulations.

The 24-combination SVM decoding matrix values in Fig. 9E were extracted from the figure as described in the text. OCR of the exact figure numeric values may be subject to reading error due to PDF quality. Extracted AUC values represent best reading from figure description in the paper.

Topographic maps (Figs. 4, 5, 9A, 9B) show spatial distributions of periodic power and aperiodic parameters but provide no coordinate tables or numeric values per electrode. Only descriptive text characterizes spatial patterns.

The paper states 'median 20-second EEG data of acupuncture' was selected, meaning the analysis window was the middle 20 seconds of the 1-minute manipulation period. This is important for understanding what the EEG data represents.

Frequency band-level p-values in Fig. 3 are presented as pairs (e.g., p=0.97; p=0.76 for delta periodic power) but the paper does not always explicitly state which pair is LT vs rest and which is TR vs rest. Based on context, the first value appears to correspond to LT vs rest and the second to TR vs rest.
No clinical behavioral outcomes (e.g., pain, symptom scales, cognitive assessments) were collected or reported. The study was purely neurophysiological with EEG.

The SVM validation method (e.g., cross-validation type, train/test split) was not described. AUC = 0.87 for alpha PW + aperiodic slope should be interpreted cautiously without knowing the validation scheme.

It is not explicitly stated whether subjects received LT and TR in separate sessions on different days, or in the same session with a washout period. The description implies a single experiment session but is ambiguous about whether both manipulations were administered to the same subjects.
